parsed.claim: For every d (including d = 0), fullQuotientSet d is bounded below by 0, so the sInf in fullLinearProgram never collapses to the junk value 0 through unboundedness below. The proof uses Fourier inversion: f(0) = ∫ 𝓕f, whose real part is nonnegative. This establishes only the BddBelow half of the check; nonemptiness and positivity of fullLinearProgram are not proved here.
parsed.lean:
theorem probe_bdd_below (d : ℕ) : BddBelow (PackingBounds.fullQuotientSet d) := by
  refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
  rintro _ ⟨f, rfl⟩
  unfold PackingBounds.fullQuotient
  refine div_nonneg ?_ f.fourier_zero_pos.le
  have h1 : (𝓕⁻ (𝓕 f.function) : CohnElkies.TestFunction d) = f.function :=
    FourierTransform.fourierInv_fourier_eq _
  have h2 : f.function 0 = ∫ v, (𝓕 f.function) v := by
    have h3 := congrFun (SchwartzMap.fourierInv_coe (𝓕 f.function)) 0
    rw [h1] at h3
    rw [h3, Real.fourierInv_eq']
    simp
  rw [h2]
  have h4 : (∫ v, (𝓕 f.function) v).re = ∫ v, ((𝓕 f.function) v).re := by
    have := integral_re (𝕜 := ℂ) (SchwartzMap.integrable (𝓕 f.function))
    simpa using this.symm
  rw [h4]
  exact integral_nonneg (fun v => f.fourier_nonneg v)
